body.estimand_functional: \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=\sum_{k=-2r}^{2r}\{\mathbb E_P[Z_0^{(1)}Z_k^{(2)}]-\tau_{\mathrm P}^2\}\), with the mean-centered test \(\phi_{n,\alpha}=\mathbf 1\{\widehat\Omega_n^{12}>t_n(\alpha)\}\); the lag-\((2r+1)\) statistic satisfies \(\mathbb E_P[\widehat\Omega_n^{\mathrm u}]=\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\).  In the canonical full-observable experiment, whose vector contains the observed graph, both assignments, both exposures, both realized outcomes, and the known propensity coordinates, \(s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\Theta(n^{-1/2})\); the score-vector radius \(s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{score}}=\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) is a corollary.  Both rates hold for distinct focal labels \(e_1\ne e_0\), fixed \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\), \(p=1/2\), and \(\alpha+\beta<1\).

sampling_model.design: Two conditionally independent Bernoulli assignment waves with known probability \(p\) are applied to the same graph, exposure mapping, and no-carryover potential-outcome schedule after a prespecified washout; the deterministic covariance cutoff and analysis interior are fixed before assignment.
sampling_model.units: The canonical specialization observes \(\Lambda_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and analyzes its buffered interior \(I_n\). The dependency-set formulation also covers deterministic F\o lner interiors of finitely generated amenable Cayley graphs under fixed local range.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary assignments in each wave generate local exposure labels and realized outcomes under one common schedule; the full minimax observation contains the finite graph, both assignments, both exposure arrays, both realized-outcome arrays, and known propensity coordinates.
sampling_model.overlap: Both focal exposures have conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\) in each wave, so every IPW division is well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Propensities are known from the design. The mean-centered statistic estimates only the two wave means, the lag-separated statistic removes that centering bias exactly, and neither procedure estimates unit-specific conditional scores or fits a regression.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 1 show that zero asymptotic variance for a stationary finite-variance finite-dependent sequence is equivalent to a finite-dependent coboundary and yields an unnormalized endpoint-difference law.
The paper proves consistency and asymptotic normality for exposure-IPW estimators under approximate neighborhood interference and studies network-HAC inference for one randomized finite population.
The paper proves central limit and invariance principles for stationary fields represented as functions of independent innovations under short-range physical dependence.
The paper proves treatment-effect asymptotics under graphon-random interference and develops direct- and indirect-effect inference.

The preprint proves asymptotic normality and optimality for regression-adjusted average-direct-effect estimators under graphon interference and consistently estimates the linear estimator's asymptotic variance under a low-rank graphon condition.

The preprint uses a first-wave pilot to estimate variance and optimizes second-wave participation and treatment assignments for average treatment and average spillover effects under network interference.

body.tldr: Two conditionally independent assignment waves on one no-carryover schedule identify the Palm population covariance through observable cross-wave IPW products. Bounded primitive influence, bounded score-dependency degree, a common Palm mean, and a fixed deterministic covariance-support pair set yield order-\(n^{-1}\) centering bias and root-\(n\) finite-sample concentration on F\o lner interiors, with the buffered integer interval giving the explicit size--power test and an exactly unbiased lag-separated version. A four-cell exact-local least-favorable schedule gives common support to the induced laws of the complete buffered graph--assignment--exposure--outcome record and proves a matching full-observation minimax lower bound. Thus, for distinct focal exposure labels, both the full-observation and score-vector separation radii are \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) for fixed \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\), \(p=1/2\), and \(\alpha+\beta<1\).

project_justification.gap: Janson2015 classifies the zero-long-run-variance boundary for finite block factors, and the one-wave interference papers study effect or estimator-variance inference. Viviano2020 already develops a two-wave network design in which a pilot estimates variance and the second wave optimizes participation and treatment; none of these works supplies a repeated-randomization test of the Palm population-covariance boundary or a full-observation minimax converse for it.
project_justification.niche: Conditional replication removes assignment noise from cross-wave IPW products. Fixed local dependency sets make the quadratic diagnostic concentrate on deterministic F\o lner interiors, while four local assignment cells leave unobserved schedule coordinates after two waves and give common support to the induced observed-data laws needed for a full-record information bound.
project_justification.fill: The project gives the cross-wave identity, order-\(n^{-1}\) centering control, root-\(n\) concentration, finite-sample size and power, and an exactly unbiased lag-separated interval statistic. For distinct focal exposure labels, it also constructs a causal-realizable four-cell submodel with \(\operatorname{KL}\le2N_ns^2\) and linearly changing \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), proving matching \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) minimax rates for the complete declared observation and, as a corollary, for the score vector.

body.related_work: Janson2015 supplies the finite-dependent coboundary result used to interpret the zero boundary, but no two-wave statistic or testing experiment. Leung2022ANI supplies one-wave exposure-IPW and approximate-neighborhood-interference analysis; no ANI or graph-HAC transfer is used here. AronowSamii2017 supplies exposure mappings and known design propensities. Viviano2020 is the closest design comparator: it uses a first-wave pilot to estimate variance and optimizes second-wave participation and treatment for average treatment and spillover effects. The present work does not claim that two-wave network designs are new; it instead uses conditionally independent replications to identify and test a Palm covariance boundary and proves a full-observation common-support minimax converse. LiWager2022 and FanLengWu2025 target causal-effect estimation and estimator variance under graphon models. Tsybakov2009 supplies the classical Pinsker and two-point testing inequalities used after the new four-cell likelihood calculation.
body.interpretation: The null \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) is a covariance-cancellation boundary, not a claim that conditional exposure effects are homogeneous. On the line, Janson's result represents the null score as a finite-block coboundary. Rejection certifies positive Palm population variation; failure to reject only places that variation within the stated finite-sample threshold.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The design requires two conditionally independent assignment waves applied to one no-carryover schedule. The full-observation converse includes the observed finite graph, assignments, exposures, realized outcomes, and known propensities, but not the innovations or unobserved assignment-cell outcomes. The graph extension requires deterministic fixed-range dependency and covariance-support sets on F\o lner interiors. No growing bandwidth, random shortest-path cutoff, approximate-neighborhood-interference transfer, endogenous graph-distance HAC, annealed CLT or Wald theorem, or BondEtAl2012 reanalysis is claimed.
body.honest_scope: The causal target is \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), the long-run covariance sum of fixed local conditional exposure-effect scores under the Palm law. The interval results and their finitely generated amenable Cayley-graph extension use a fixed deterministic local cutoff, bounded outcomes, overlap, two conditionally independent waves, bounded primitive influence, bounded score dependency, and a common Palm mean. For distinct focal exposure labels, minimax sharpness holds for the explicitly encoded finite observed-data vector at \(p=1/2\) and \(\alpha+\beta<1\); the score-vector theorem is a corollary. The note claims neither novelty of two-wave designs nor validity for richer observations that reveal innovations or unobserved potential outcomes.
